cards.q: Resonance is part of which bonding theory?
What does resonance describe in valence bond theory?
cards.a: Delocalised electron systems, in terms of contributing structures.

cards.q: What kind of bonds does each contributing resonance structure involve?
Do individual resonance structures exist on their own in rapid equilibrium?
cards.a: No; they do not exist on their own and are not in any rapid equilibrium.

cards.q: Must resonance contributing structures be equally weighted?
cards.a: No; they do not have to be equally weighted in their contribution.

cards.q: Which molecule is given as an example of genuine rapid interconversion that is not called resonance?
For the 2-norbornyl cation, which structure did X-ray diffraction show to be correct?
In what year was an X-ray diffraction structure of the 2-norbornyl cation obtained?
In amides, what does resonance imply for the C–N bond order?
cards.a: It is greater than 1, giving the bond some double bond character.

cards.q: In amides, what does resonance imply for the C–O bond order?
On a potential energy diagram, how does a resonance hybrid differ from equilibrating structures?
cards.a: A resonance hybrid is a single potential energy minimum; equilibrating structures are two minima separated by a barrier.

cards.q: What is the alternative to the valence bond and resonance description of delocalised bonding?
cards.a: Molecular orbital theory, in which electrons occupy molecular orbitals extending over more than two atoms.
